findings.title: Hosts without qualification records remain admitted with a null gate
findings.trigger: A Packet selects Claude, Codex, OpenCode, Kimi, or Grok, whose current profiles have no enforcement qualification record.
findings.impact: A future caller that treats route admitted as factory qualification can launch a Host without dimension evidence. This is retained for legacy N=1 compatibility and does not block the current unavailable ZCode route.
findings.evidence: Only ZCode currently registers an enforcement record, host decisions add a gate only when a record exists, and tests explicitly lock the other five Hosts to admitted, gate null, and empty qualified dimensions.
findings.suggestion: Require gate enforcement_qualification at the future factory entry and qualify each Host and transport before admitting it there; do not change the current legacy N=1 behavior in D1.

findings.title: Installed diagnostics reference Host evidence that the npm package does not ship
findings.trigger: An npm-installed runtime returns the unavailable ZCode diagnostic and the user follows its evidence reference.
findings.impact: The typed diagnostic points at a source-repository-only .ultra evidence path, so installed users cannot inspect the exact receipt and the runtime policy remains coupled to development-repository provenance.
findings.evidence: The retained profile embeds .ultra/evidence/vnext-d1-host-enforcement-qualification/host-enforcement-receipt.json, while the package allowlist omits .ultra and current tests validate that reference only from the source checkout.
findings.suggestion: Before publication that relies on this diagnostic, ship a redacted digest-bound receipt as a Skill or documentation asset and test its presence in the real tarball, or point the reference to an equivalent immutable shipped artifact.

findings.title: Qualification identity compares expected constants instead of a concrete observed candidate
findings.trigger: A future positive qualification is retained and a candidate is later replaced by another build that reports the same marker and version.
findings.impact: Admission can match profile constants without proving that the selected binary is the artifact observed by the qualification receipt.
findings.evidence: The retained receipt contains a concrete artifact digest, but qualified_identity and the admission decision consume expected marker and version constants rather than that artifact identity; the live probe validates the same marker and version.
findings.suggestion: For a future positive qualification, bind the concrete candidate path and immutable digest or an equivalent strong identity into the selection observation and exact transport admission.

findings.title: Host-created sessions or process groups can escape the portable writer observation
findings.trigger: A Host or adapter daemonizes, calls setsid, or moves the real writer into a new process group before the original child or group exits.
findings.impact: The recorded PID and process group can appear stopped while an escaped writer still writes. The current ZCode route is unavailable, and other legacy routes are not claimed as factory-qualified by this D1 smoke.
findings.evidence: The writer observation records one child PID and process group, and liveness and termination inspect only that group; no portable OS primitive proves arbitrary session descendants remain contained.
findings.suggestion: Require lifecycle qualification for every Host entering the factory and keep an unprovable route unavailable; add OS containment such as Job Objects or cgroups only when a real qualified Host requires it.

findings.title: Start identity is weaker on non-Linux platforms
findings.trigger: A PID is reused or an outer-worker start identity cannot be obtained on macOS or Windows.
findings.impact: Recovery must conservatively retain alive or unknown and may freeze a lock or fence until manual reconciliation. It does not currently misreport stopped, so this is a bounded availability risk.
findings.evidence: processStartIdentity returns a non-null start identity only from Linux procfs; other platforms retain the weaker liveness fallback and fail closed when identity proof is unavailable.
findings.suggestion: Add platform-native start identity or Job Object support only after measured recovery cost justifies it; keep the current conservative unknown behavior.

findings.title: The fence registry lock can remain stale after launcher crash
findings.trigger: The launcher crashes or is forcibly killed after creating the registry lock directory and before its finally cleanup.
findings.impact: Later fence acquire and release operations time out as registry busy and require manual recovery, reducing local delegation availability.
findings.evidence: The lock directory has no owner PID or start identity and no proven-dead recovery path; cleanup relies on the creating process reaching finally.
findings.suggestion: Only after a real incident, bind the registry lock to owner and start identity and permit proven-dead cleanup; never delete it by an unverified TTL.

findings.title: The ZCode bridge command selector remains visible to the final Host
findings.trigger: A future ZCode route is admitted and the final Host receives the selected-Host environment.
findings.impact: The final Host sees ULTRA_ZCODE_ACP_COMMAND after launcher command resolution has already consumed it. It is not a secret and the current route is unavailable.
findings.evidence: The key participates in command selection and remains on the ZCode Host allowlist; the retained receipt includes it among Host environment key names.
findings.suggestion: After a positive route exists, keep the selector at probe or launcher scope and omit it from the final Host environment unless the runtime proves it is needed there.

positive_observations: The exact ZCode route is rejected before executable identity probes, fences, worker specs, workers, or Hosts, with no hidden fallback or repeat provider call.
descendant Host environments are rebuilt from digest-bound keys and values instead of merging the full Primary process environment.
No Run Supervisor, wake, graph controller, automatic retry, or new dependency entered the D1 subject.
limitations: The review made no live provider call and used the frozen receipt for current ZCode facts.
Fake process fixtures cannot prove macOS or Windows lifecycle containment or exclude Host-created session escape.
The review stayed inside the immutable packet diff scope and did not inspect unrelated dirty paths as findings.
